To: Executive Leadership and Regional Operations
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: As of this memo
Subject: Aligning network shipments to meet all demand at the lowest delivered cost

Situation
We operate a broad network of warehouses, factories, and distribution centers serving a dispersed set of stores, customers, and regional hubs. Freight rates differ by lane, and service expectations remain high. To control spend without compromising on-time delivery, we need a clear, lane-by-lane shipping plan that uses our available inventory efficiently. Shipments must be in whole-unit increments; partial loads are not permitted.

Problem
We need to determine how much to ship from each source to each destination so that:
- No source dispatches more than its available inventory or capacity.
- Every destination receives the full quantity required.
- The overall transportation spend is as low as possible given varying route costs.

This requires a coordinated allocation across the network that respects source limits, fulfills destination needs, and prioritizes lower-cost lanes where practical. The outcome will guide our routing instructions, carrier assignments, and weekly dispatch schedules, helping us avoid last-minute expedites and unnecessary handling, while protecting customer service.

Next steps
- Validate the current availability at each source and required quantities at each destination.
- Use the lane cost data to develop a shipment allocation that meets all needs at the lowest total delivered cost.
- Confirm that the plan adheres to whole-unit shipping requirements and operational cutoffs.
- Review trade-offs where lower-cost lanes may have longer lead times, and set clear exceptions for critical demand.
- Publish the recommended routing guide and transition plan, with monitoring to track adherence and savings.
